notes.meaning: Jesus warns that people everywhere will hate His followers because they belong to Him. The hatred is really aimed at Him, and that is a comfort. The troubles will not last forever, and God holds His people up while they last. Those who keep going with Him to the very end will be saved and share fully in His kingdom.

differ.view: Holding on to the end is the mark of a true believer. No true child of God can lose salvation, and those who fall away show they were never truly rescued.
The verse is a real warning: those who do not hold on to faith and a good conscience until death have no hope of entering God's kingdom.

notes.meaning: When one town turns against them, the disciples may move on to the next and keep preaching. They must not throw their lives away. But they also must never deny Christ or use wrong means to escape. Many older writers read 'before the Son of Man comes' as Christ coming in judgment on Jerusalem. Others read it as His rising from the dead or the coming of the Holy Spirit.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some modern writers say that, taken at face value, Jesus predicted something that did not happen. They add that the saying is so surprising that no one would have made it up.

notes.meaning: A student does not rank above his teacher, and a servant does not rank above his master. Jesus is our Teacher and Lord. So His followers should not expect to be treated better than He was.

It is honor enough for a follower to share his Master's lot. Jesus' enemies called Him Beelzebul, a name for the prince of demons. That was the worst insult they could think of. If they said that about the Head of the house, His family can be sure to hear the same.

So the disciples need not fear their enemies. One day everything hidden will be brought into the open. The good news will spread everywhere. The innocence of God's slandered servants will be shown, if not in this life, then on the last day.

What Jesus taught them in private, they must announce in public. Houses then had flat roofs, which were open, high places for making things known. No part of Jesus' message is to be kept back. They are to share the whole of it boldly.

People can kill the body, but that is the limit of their power. They cannot touch the soul. The One to fear is God, who alone can destroy both body and soul in hell. A healthy awe of God is the best cure for fear of people.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: A few scholars have thought the One to fear here is the devil, the tempter, rather than God.

notes.meaning: Sparrows were so cheap that two sold for one small coin. Yet not one falls to the ground without God knowing and allowing it. God's care, called his 'providence,' reaches even the smallest creatures.

God even keeps count of the hairs on your head. This is a picture of how closely He watches over every detail of His people's lives. It is not given for curious guessing. It is given so we will trust His fatherly care.
For the third time in a few verses, Jesus says, 'Do not be afraid.' If God cares for sparrows, He cares far more for His children. Persecuted people may feel forgotten, but they are not.

To 'confess' Jesus means to openly say we belong to Him, in our words and in how we live. Jesus promises that He will gladly own such a person before His Father in heaven. We honor Him before people, which is a small thing. He honors us before God, which is a great thing.

Whoever disowns Jesus before people will be disowned by Him before the Father. The sources say this means a lasting, settled denial. It does not mean a moment of weakness that is later repented of, like Peter's. It is a very serious warning.

Many expected the Messiah to bring outward peace and good times. Jesus says His coming will bring a 'sword,' meaning division and conflict. That is the result of His coming, not its goal. People's opposition to Him causes the conflict. He does bring true peace with God, but not an easy peace in this world.

Jesus uses words from the prophet Micah. When some in a family follow Him and others do not, even the closest family ties can break. Sometimes a believer's worst opponents are in their own home. This is not the gospel's fault, and it does not always happen. But when it does, believers should not be alarmed.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: One Catholic reading sees a deeper, spiritual meaning. God's word cuts the new person off from old sin in baptism, which causes conflict 'in one house.' The daughter-in-law against the mother-in-law is read as the Church against the Synagogue.

notes.meaning: Jesus must be loved most of all, even above parents and children. He does not tell us to stop loving our families. He puts that love in its right place, below Him. To 'take up your cross' means being ready to suffer, even to die, for Him. It also means bearing the hard things that come with obeying Him, following His example.

The word 'life' has two senses here: life in this world and eternal life. Someone who saves his earthly life by denying Christ will lose eternal life. Someone who is willing to give up his life for Christ will gain eternal life. Those who hold this life loosely are best prepared for the next.

Jesus counts any kindness shown to His messengers as shown to Himself. Welcoming Him also means welcoming the Father who sent Him. It is like an ambassador: how he is treated shows how his king is regarded.

A 'prophet' here is someone sent by God with His message, like a preacher of the gospel. Whoever welcomes such a person, or a godly person, because they serve God will share in their reward. What matters is doing it for Christ's sake.

The 'little ones' are Jesus' ordinary, humble followers whom the world looks down on. Even the smallest kindness, like a cup of cold water, given because they belong to Christ, will not go unnoticed. God values the love behind a gift, not its cost. The sources stress that the reward comes as God's free gift, not as something we earn.
